big_idea: Detectives predict the MODE for one group, then test in ANOTHER group. Same mode? Different?
learning_intention: We are learning to predict mode and test across groups.
student_learning_goal: I can predict mode and test it across groups.
success_criteria: I can SURVEY 5 children in one group.
I can TEST the same survey in a different group.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Lucky and Mae — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.activity_name: Lucky and Mae Plan the Capstone
minds_on.hook: Lucky: Today's CASE — predict the MODE in one group, then TEST in another. Same? Different? Lucky+Mae open: 'Same die, different ROLLS! Different MODES! PREDICTION uses the DATA!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Lucky and Mae puppets in lab coats. 'Friends — today our CAPSTONE. We use ALL we know: likelihood, complementary, spinner, dice, MODE prediction.'

Review: 'Step 1 — pick a question. Step 2 — survey 5 in our class. Step 3 — find mode. Step 4 — predict mode in another group. Step 5 — test if right.'

Demo. Class data: 'Favourite snack: apple 2, cookie 3, sandwich 0. Mode = COOKIE.'

'Predict another class — will MODE be cookie too? Maybe. Maybe not. Different group, different favourites.'

Now show the 5 stations:
- Station 1: LIKELIHOOD — sort 6 events I/P/C.
- Station 2: COMPLEMENT — match 4 complement pairs.
- Station 3: SPINNER — predict + test 5 spins.
- Station 4: DICE MODE — roll 12 times, find mode.
- Station 5: SURVEY — survey 5 classmates, find mode, predict for another group.

Each child rotates and records on TEMPLATE.

'Lucky says — every detective uses ALL these skills.'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 5 stations rotation (~5 min each).

COMPARE TWO PREDICTIONS: Present 'Lin says SAME mode because both classes used the same die'; 'Sam says DIFFERENT mode because each set is fresh.' Class debates with data — both can be right depending on sample size. Cite Konold (2002) — process vs realised data distinction.
steps.teacher_prompt: Mae: 'Sometimes both children are right. Long-run mode = same. Short-run mode = could differ.'

differentiation.for_extending: After all 5, write a 'big idea' conclusion.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 5 station tables physically. NO-PAPER VERSION: 5 corners of the room as stations (Likelihood corner, Complement corner, Spinner corner, Dice corner, Mode-Prediction corner). Children rotate through corners, class records on chart paper.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: likelihood; complement; spinner; dice mode; survey + predict.

discussion_prompts: Did your prediction match the test?
Why might mode differ between groups?
consolidation.exit_routine: Closing capstone refrain — Lucky+Mae call-and-response: Lucky: 'Same die, different ROLLS!' Mae: 'Different MODES!' Class: 'PREDICTION uses the DATA!' (3x). Each child reads one mode prediction with the data citation.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 5 captures D2.1 + D2.2 in one lab.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child predicts SAME mode for new group — repairing the same-mode-different-group trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On mode prediction across two populations (Day 5 capstone), the trap is mode-as-property-of-the-DATA vs mode-as-property-of-the-GROUP-PROCESS confusion (Konold 2002, 'Teaching Concepts Fundamentally', and Lehrer & Schauble 2002 'Investigating Real Data'): child says 'same fair die produces SAME MODE in both classes' (true on average over thousands of rolls; false in small samples). The fix: distinguish the underlying process from the realised data.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: likelihood (L1), complement (L2), spinner-proportion (L3), dice-fairness (L4) into a mode-prediction capstone.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone Station 5. Child surveyed own class: cookie mode. Predicts another class will ALSO have cookie mode.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Your class mode was cookie. But Lucky asks — could ANOTHER class have a different mode?'

Guide. 'Different groups = different favourites. Maybe Ms. B's class loves apples. Maybe Mr. C's loves sandwich.'

Generlise. 'Mode is GROUP-specific. Predict THIS group, test THAT group, accept differences.'

If still rigidly predicting same: provide a 3-group comparison sample.
common_misconceptions: Different groups won't differ. (Repair: they often do.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child says SAME MODE because 'same die': name the variability — 'same die, different ROLLS, different MODES in small samples.'
DIAGNOSTIC B — child knows variability but can't articulate: force the sentence frame 'Class A's mode and Class B's mode MIGHT be the same OR different because each set of 20 rolls is FRESH.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child makes a prediction but won't justify with data citation: highlight the data table, ask 'show me the ROW your prediction comes from.'

parts_outline.task: Sort 4 events I/P/C and identify a complement.
Predict + test a spinner. Roll dice 10 times, find mode.
Survey 5 classmates. Find mode. Predict mode for ANOTHER group.
